scoreRule: 1 point per correct MC item; 10 points maximum; local provisional grade only
description: Original English A2 reading-test draft about Daniel's plan and reasons for improving.

tabs.title: Reasons and Results
tabs.description: Connect what Daniel does with why it helps.

tabs.title: Using the Learning Strategy
tabs.description: Apply the idea in other classes.

questions.q: What does Daniel want to change before his next science test?
choices: The time of the science lesson.
The subject of the science test.
How he prepares during the week.
The teacher who marks the paper.
questions.explanation: In paragraph one, Daniel identifies his late-night studying as a problem and wants a different plan.

questions.q: Why is Wednesday evening a problem in Daniel's usual routine?
choices: He always meets his friends that evening.
He studies late and feels tired the next day.
His sister needs the room for music.
He forgets to take his textbook home.
questions.explanation: In paragraph one, Daniel identifies his late-night studying as a problem and wants a different plan.

questions.q: When does Daniel try questions without looking at the answers?
choices: On Monday, after a short break.
On Friday, after school.
On Thursday, during the test.
On Wednesday, before the test.
questions.explanation: Paragraph two describes short sessions, explaining ideas, looking at notes and answering questions independently.

questions.q: Why does Daniel ask his sister about a topic?
choices: Explaining it can show what he does not understand.
She can answer the science test for him.
His teacher asks her to give him a mark.
He wants to avoid looking at his notes.
questions.explanation: Paragraph two describes short sessions, explaining ideas, looking at notes and answering questions independently.

questions.q: What does Daniel do after he finds a difficult idea?
choices: He stops all his preparation.
He changes the date of the test.
He checks his notes and looks for help.
He copies his sister's answers.
questions.explanation: Paragraph two describes short sessions, explaining ideas, looking at notes and answering questions independently.

questions.q: What matters to Daniel besides his slightly better grade?
choices: He feels calmer and has enough rest.
He finishes his test earlier than everyone.
He studies without ever making a mistake.
His sister has learnt his science textbook.
questions.explanation: Paragraph three connects his calmer result with reflection and plans for future subjects.

questions.q: Why does Daniel write down what to practise after the test?
choices: He wants to change all his answers.
He wants to know what he can improve next.
He has already forgotten the test date.
He wants to study the same facts forever.
questions.explanation: Paragraph three connects his calmer result with reflection and plans for future subjects.

questions.q: You cannot explain a new word to a partner. Which step is closest to Daniel's strategy?
choices: Give up on the topic immediately.
Pretend you understand the word.
Read only the correct answer without thinking.
Check your notes and then try explaining it again.
questions.explanation: Paragraph two describes short sessions, explaining ideas, looking at notes and answering questions independently.

questions.q: Why might Daniel use his plan for history next week?
choices: His science teacher also teaches history.
He thinks a useful routine can work in another subject.
He has no other homework.
The history test uses exactly the same questions.
questions.explanation: Paragraph three connects his calmer result with reflection and plans for future subjects.

questions.q: Which student has a plan most like Daniel's?
choices: A student who stays up all night before each test.
A student who only reads answers without practising.
A student who never changes a plan that fails.
A student who studies in short sessions and checks progress.
questions.explanation: Paragraph three connects his calmer result with reflection and plans for future subjects.
